svg.font-family: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, 'Segoe UI', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Nightseam 0.6.0 — the projection stages and their interfaces
svg.desc: The consumer writes a declaration in no language and a program per language: a model of its side as its own functions, and the composition root that picks a transport, makes a peer, composes the layers and calls ToWire and FromWire. The declaration is rendered into a Go and a TypeScript realization: the family in the language — its types, its two models as records of native functions, its identity — and the sides' adapters, one package per declared side, which present a model as a wire and a wire as a model; both generated. Beneath them the library, written once per language: the wire is Bitwire's shared access contract — Wire, Endpoint and Receiver — owned outside both realizations; each realizes it with its peer's endpoint, its channels and its model endpoints, and composes a dispatcher above it. The live and tunnel layers compose over the peer; the peer speaks the profile's frames over a connection of the seam. The two realizations meet at the frames on the wire. Each row is tagged by who provides it: the consumer, the generator, Nightseam's library, or a language-agnostic definition. A connection, a channel, a selection, a mount and a forward are each a wire again.
svg.text: one declaration, one contract, one profile — each shared, each realized twice; every layer speaks the one beneath it and knows nothing of those above
CONSUMER — written by the consumer: a declaration in no language, and a program per language · GENERATED — rendered per family from the declaration into the consumer's tree, by nightseam generate
LIBRARY — written once per language and shipped by Nightseam: duplex, runtime, live, tunnel · AGNOSTIC — one definition in no language, drawn across both columns

Bitwire 0.2.0 — the access contract, owned by Bitspark/bitwire; named directly in every language, never copied, aliased or re-exported
Wire { send(path, message) } · Endpoint extends Wire { receive(receiver) → detach, close(code, reason) } · Receiver { message(path, message), closed(code, reason) }
a ReturnAddress carries send-only Wire; one owning receive attachment per Endpoint; registration, prefix routing and precedence are a composed dispatcher's, not the contract's

nightseam.duplex/1 — the frames of the profile, over a WebSocket, a pipe or a tunnel channel
what crosses: request · response · event · cancel, with the meta header and trace context; the reserved vocabularies channel.* live.* identity.* as ordinary frames;
request serials that increase per direction; the declaration's digest at channel.open, at identity.check and on a transferred reference — never a path member, never a lifecycle verb
the recurrence — and where the layers meet it
a connection is a wire at [] · a tunnel channel is a wire, being a connection of the seam · at(w, p), mount({…}) and forward(w) yield a wire again
a model adapter targets a wire — ToWire(model) → Endpoint, FromWire(endpoint) → model — so a selected part and an assembled whole are used the same way
a live reference names a binding in a scope, beside the wire, under an owner the caller supplies; the conformance suite holds every language to this one definition
